notes:
Context: Verdant Orbit runs omnichannel CX platform for 150+ mid-market customers. Primary concern = reliability during incident bursts & seasonal peaks (Black Friday / product launches). Current stack: inbound queues -> rules router -> agent UI + async ticket backend. They want LLMs for agent_assist (real-time reply suggestions), ticket_summarization (end-of-shift), and tool_calling (create tickets, escalate).

Requirements (copied from call):
- Latency target: p95 <= 600ms for agent assist in normal load; must degrade gracefully under burst (no >5s hard failures).
- Throughput baseline: 240 qps for agent assist across cluster; peak multipliers up to 8-12x during seasonal spikes.
- Cost sensitivity: bounded per-conversation cost; prefer routing lower-cost quantized model for lower-fidelity answers during overflow.
- Reliability: deterministic fallbacks when primary model exhausted; preference for Dedicated pool + autoscale with max burst capacity.
- Observability & audit: token-level cost, per-request trace ids, and audit logs for compliance. KMS integration required.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, retention controls, and EU data residency for some customers.

POC notes (shorthand):
- POC run 1: used hosted_api, sample traffic replay from 2024 holiday set. Observed queue backpressure at 4x baseline -> request timeouts and reroute loops.
- SE suggestion: enable prefix caching for frequent prompts, continuous batching with latency buckets, and model variant routing (gpt-like-high -> small-quantized) when queue length exceeds threshold.
- They want an SLA-like target for tail latency and a documented fallback chain.

Quotes / sales snippets:
- "We can absorb small blips but not 10s of seconds — agents go blind." (Head of Ops)
- "If you can show consistent 99th percentile behavior under realistic holiday traffic we'll move to a reserved contract."
